events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.55)
events.body: The cancellation is a driver cancellation with the driver asserting a rider no-show, so the case enters through NS-0 and is governed by NS-1 [F5]. NS-1 requires all three elements together: a driver "I'm Here" tap, GPS placing the driver within the pickup radius at that tap, and a continuous wait in that radius for more than 3 minutes up to the cancellation [F7][F6]. The trace marks NS-1 as failed because the GPS trace does not cover the wait: no samples exist between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, a 3 min 20 s gap [F1], and per G12/NS-1 the interval between two samples is not a measured wait. The remaining elements look supportive — platform arrival at 14:21:15, tap at 14:22:15 at 39 m, 4 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap and a stationary 5 min 0 s block at 39 m [F2][F3][F4][F6][F7] — but the closure of that waiting period rests on samples that the gap interrupts, so the record does not settle whether the driver waited continuously past the 3-minute threshold before cancelling [F1][F5]. Because the undisturbed wait is a record a clause needs and it is missing, this is insufficiency of evidence rather than a finding for either side, and the only permitted outcome is escalation [F1][NS-1]. The rider's one-minute-late account and the driver's "waited over 3 minutes" statement are both statements, which cannot override the missing movement record [F13][F5]. The traffic and weather facts are irrelevant here: the dispute is a no-show fee, not a route deviation, and no incident was recorded [F14][F15][F16]. Profiles are not decisive and are not used to rule [F17][F18]. On safety, I read both chat messages ("I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6", "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel"), the driver's written statement and the complaint: there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is clear [F10][F11][F13].
